newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope urges reconciliation ahead of Lebanon trip.
newsitem.headline: Pope urges reconciliation ahead of Lebanon trip.

text.p: Pope John Paul, who travels to Beirut later this month, on Friday urged the people of Lebanon to work together to rebuild their war-shattered state.

"I entrust to Almighty God the courageous march of the Lebanese people on the path of national reconciliation and social reconstruction," the Pontiff said in a message to the Lebanese people, referring to the devastating 1975-90 civil war.
"I trust in you to find in the love for your country the necessary energy to conquer divisions and surmouNt any obstacles which might arise," he said ahead of his May 10-11 visit.
The Vatican postponed a five-day visit to Lebanon scheduled for May 1994 after the bombing of a Maronite church north of Beirut that killed 11 Sunday worshippers and injured 59.
During his trip, the first by a Pope to Lebanon in modern times, the Pontiff will preside over the ceremonial ending of a synod of the Lebanese Church held at the Vatican in 1995.
The trip also includes mass and a meeting with young people.
The Polish Pope, who often calls for Middle East peace and dreams of visiting the Holy Land by the year 2000, is also expected to urge a comprehensive settlement in the region.
